title: Hosea: betrothed again (Hosea 2:16–22)
hookLine: a broken marriage restored becomes a picture of God and Israel

lines: A PROPHET IS TOLD TO MARRY.
cards: The first thing Hosea is asked to do is marry. He marries Gomer, and the marriage goes wrong. In the chapters that follow, the book speaks of a wife who goes after other lovers, and it doesn't look away from the hurt.
Children with names that sound like verdicts. Anger, accusation, a house gone cold. A story could end there.
This one doesn't. Somewhere in the middle of the second chapter, the voice changes, and a door opens in the wall.

teach.h: A MARRIAGE AS A PICTURE OF COVENANT.
teach.b: Hosea's marriage becomes a picture of God and Israel: a covenant like a wedding, a people who wandered after other gods, a love that's been wounded. And in chapter two, God speaks like a husband who wants to begin again.

teach.h: BACK TO THE WILDERNESS, SPOKEN TO GENTLY.
teach.b: In the 1917 Jewish translation: "I will allure her, And bring her into the wilderness, And speak tenderly unto her."

The wilderness, not as punishment, but as the place where the first love began, after Egypt, before all the trouble. The valley of Achor, remembered for an old trouble, becomes, the text says, "a door of hope."
Then a small, sharp change of names. On that day, the text says, you will call me Ishi, my husband, and no more Baali.

Baali can also mean my husband, but it echoes the god Baal, and the next verse says the names of the Baalim will be taken out of her mouth. The bond is to be personal again, not one more lord among lords.

teach.h: I WILL BETROTH THEE UNTO ME FOR EVER.
teach.b: Then the vows, in the 1917 Jewish translation: "And I will betroth thee unto Me for ever; Yea, I will betroth thee unto Me in righteousness, and in justice, And in lovingkindness, and in compassion. And I will betroth thee unto Me in faithfulness."
Betroth, three times. Not remarried: betrothed, as if engaged for the first time. And the gifts aren't jewelry.
They're righteousness, justice, lovingkindness, compassion, faithfulness.

teach.h: SAID WHILE WINDING THE TEFILLIN STRAP.
teach.b: Some Jews say these lines each weekday morning, while winding the tefillin strap around the finger, like a ring.

how: Jews who wear tefillin often recite Hosea 2:21–22 on weekday mornings while winding the tefillin strap around the middle finger, and the verses are part of the haftarah for the Torah portion Bamidbar.

o: a judge who led the tribes after Joshua's death
the prophet whose broken marriage pictures the covenant
a priest who served in the Temple Solomon built

s: in Hosea, the broken marriage ends the story
chapter two turns, and God promises to betroth the people again.
the wilderness here is only a place of punishment
God says, I will allure her, bring her into the wilderness, and speak tenderly unto her.
the betrothal gifts are righteousness, justice, lovingkindness, compassion and faithfulness
no jewelry. the gifts are ways of keeping faith.

games.q: the marriage in Hosea has broken. in chapter two, what does God say comes next?
o: a new betrothal, as if from the beginning.
games.why: God says, I will betroth thee unto Me for ever, three times over: a fresh start, not a patched one.

practice: Bring to mind one person you've drifted from or grown used to, a partner, a parent, a friend, a sibling, and go back in your mind to the wilderness, to the beginning, when it was new: what did you first notice and like about them?
Then ask which word from Hosea's list this bond needs most: justice, kindness, compassion or faithfulness. If you pray, you can say the betrothal line slowly.

wordCard.voice: Hosea. The prophet whose broken marriage becomes a picture of God and Israel, and who hears God promise to betroth the people again. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: and I will betroth you to Me, the opening of the vows in Hosea 2:21.

carryVoice: Your line: betrothed again. Back to the beginning, as if for the first time. See you tomorrow.
